# Scholars Reading List search API

> Search ~200 million scholarly papers (OpenAlex titles and abstracts) by meaning or by exact words, find
> papers similar to a given one, look a paper up by DOI / OpenAlex id / PMCID, walk its citations, and map
> the research groups inside a topic with what to read in each.
> Read-only JSON over HTTPS, no key. Built for ScienceMadeReadable; open to anyone's programs and agents.

Base URL: https://api.sciencemadereadable.com/api/data
(On Maxime's machines: http://127.0.0.1:8810 on lambda itself, https://lambda.tail69222b.ts.net:18810 on
the tailnet. Same API and the same data, without the public rate limit.)

Interactive reference (every parameter, try it in the browser): <base>/docs · machine-readable: <base>/openapi.json
This guide: <base>/llms.txt

Only able to open a web address (no code, no headers)? Put the question in the address and get the answer as
plain text: https://ask.sciencemadereadable.com/why do cats purr, or <base>/search/why do cats purr (spaces as %20
or +; options after ?, e.g. ?k=30&year_from=2020). The research groups of a topic, the same way:
https://ask.sciencemadereadable.com/map/intermittent fasting, or <base>/topics/intermittent fasting.

Using an AI app that speaks MCP (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Codex...)? Add the MCP server
https://api.sciencemadereadable.com/mcp instead: the same search as tools, no key (see "MCP server" below).

## What is covered right now

- Search by meaning, every paper: 125,148,125 papers published from 1007-04-01.
- Search by meaning, papers ScienceMadeReadable can open (collection=smr): 3,902,396 papers published from 1939-10-30.
- Search by exact words and paper lookup (/works): 203,742,913 papers, all years.
- Data release 20261014T073821Z, published 2026-10-14T09:41:14Z.
- OpenAlex snapshot of 2026-10-05 (titles, abstracts, citations, labels).
- Plus 256,878 papers OpenAlex added since, fetched daily (last fetch 2026-10-14). Their citation counts and labels are as of that fetch; the citation walk does not include them yet.

## Quick start

```sh
B=https://api.sciencemadereadable.com/api/data
curl -G "$B/search" --data-urlencode "q=does intermittent fasting help weight loss" -d k=5 -d abstracts=false
curl -G "$B/search" --data-urlencode 'q="gut microbiome" AND (autism OR ASD) NOT mice' -d k=5
curl "$B/works/10.1126/science.aan8048"            # by DOI (also W123..., PMC123..., https://doi.org/...)
curl "$B/similar/W2782456798?k=5&abstracts=false"
curl "$B/walk?id=10.1126/science.aan8048&k=30"      # what papers like this one cite that it does not
curl -G "$B/topics" --data-urlencode "q=intermittent fasting for weight loss"   # research groups + reading lists
```

```python
import requests
B = "https://api.sciencemadereadable.com/api/data"
r = requests.get(f"{B}/search", params={"q": "microplastics in human placenta", "k": 20,
                                        "year_from": 2020, "abstracts": "false"}, timeout=30)
r.raise_for_status()
for p in r.json()["results"]:
    print(p["year"], p["citations"], p["title"], p["doi"] or p["openalex"])
```

## Endpoints

### GET /search/{question}
The same search for tools that can only open an address: the question is the rest of the path, the answer is
plain text (Markdown): each result's title, year, venue, authors, citations, link and abstract. Spaces as
`%20` or `+` (a `+` counts as a space only when the address has no `%20`). Takes the options of /search after
`?` (k, mode, year_from, year_to, type, open_access, license, pmc_open_access, collection, abstracts).
`https://api.sciencemadereadable.com/api/data/search/does%20intermittent%20fasting%20help%20weight%20loss?k=5`

### GET /search?q=...
The main entry. Returns `{"mode", "results": [...], "filters", "timing", ...}`.

- `q` (2–2000 characters). Plain language works: "why do cats purr", or a paragraph.
- `mode` = `auto` (default) | `semantic` | `keyword`.
  - **semantic** (by meaning): finds papers about the idea even without the same words. Best for questions
    and descriptions. Answers carry `ranking` (how they were ordered).
  - **keyword** (exact words, English stemming): plain words are ANDed; `"exact phrase"`, `OR`, `NOT` or
    `-word`, brackets, `word*`, `"a b"~5` (within 5 words), `title:`, `abstract:`, `keywords:`. Answers carry
    `matches` (exact count of matching papers) and `query` (how it was understood).
  - **auto** picks keyword when `q` contains search syntax (quotes, AND/OR/NOT in capitals, brackets, `*`,
    `-word`, `field:`), else semantic. If an auto keyword search matches nothing it searches by meaning and
    says so in `fallback`.
- `k` results, 1–100 (default 10). There is no paging: ask for up to 100 at once.
- Filters: `year_from`, `year_to`, `type` (article, review, preprint, book, book-chapter, conference-paper,
  dissertation, report, letter, editorial, ...), `open_access=true`, `license` (e.g. `cc-by`),
  `pmc_open_access=true` (full text in PubMed Central's open-access set).
- `collection` = `all` (default) | `smr`: only papers ScienceMadeReadable can open and rewrite (PubMed
  Central, CC BY, research articles).
- `abstracts=false` drops abstracts from the answer (about 10x smaller). Use it unless you need them.
- `junk_penalty` (semantic only): ranking is similarity − junk_penalty × `junk`; default 0.3 for `all`,
  0 for `smr`. 0 = pure similarity.
- `map=true` adds each result's position on the map of science (`x`, `y`, both 0–1) and where the
  question lands (`map`).

Identical records appear once; a preprint and its published version are different records and can both
appear (merge by `doi` or title if that matters). Left out unless you ask with `type=`: datasets, figures, covers and other non-publications. Always left out:
retracted papers (OpenAlex flag, or titles starting "[RETRACTED]" / "Retraction Note:").

### GET /similar/{ref}
Papers closest in meaning to one paper. `ref` = W-number, DOI or PMCID. Same `k`, filters, `abstracts`,
`collection` and `junk_penalty` as /search. 404 if the paper is not in the semantic index (see coverage).

### GET /works/{ref}
One paper's full record (fields below). `ref` = `W2782456798`, `https://openalex.org/W...`, a DOI
(`10.1126/science.aan8048`, `https://doi.org/...`, `doi:...`) or a PMCID (`PMC1234567`). 404 if unknown.

### GET /walk?id=...
A citation walk from one paper (W-number or DOI): the papers that cite most of the same references (`k`
of them, default 30) and, among what *they* cite, what the starting paper does not: `answers` (W-numbers)
are the strongest candidates for "what this paper should also have cited / what to read next". Also
returns `nodes` (title, year, citations, topic per paper), `columns`, `links` (citation edges), `stats`.
Papers listing more than `max_refs` (300) references or with more than `max_cites` (500) citations count
as outliers. Slow: 0.5–5 s. Fails with an `error` when the paper has no references in the snapshot.

### GET /topics?q=...   ·   GET /topics/{question} (plain text)
A topic map: the research groups inside a topic, and what to read in each. The `papers` (default 1000,
200–2000) closest in meaning to `q` (or the best matches of exact-words syntax; `mode` as in /search;
`year_from`, `year_to`) are grouped by the works they cite and the words they use (shared references
weighted by rarity + nearest neighbours in meaning, half each; Leiden, consensus of 20 runs). Answer:
- `groups`: `id`, `name` (the phrases most over-represented in the group, automatic), `size`, `years`
  (10th/50th/90th percentile), `typical` (its most central paper), `centre` (map position), `cites_groups`
  ({group id: citations from this group's papers to that group's}), `between` (papers whose group changes
  between runs), `openalex_topics`, and `lenses`, each a list of papers with a `why`:
  `core` (what the group cites most), `distinctive` (cited mostly by this group), `rising` (works of the
  last 5 years already cited by several of its papers), `start_here` (recent group papers citing most of its
  key works, often reviews), `bridges` (group papers whose links go largely to another group), `newest`,
  `experts` (authors by a position-weighted h-index inside the group: h of their works each cited by ≥ h
  group papers, first author full credit, last author half; OpenAlex's disambiguated authors).
  Papers in lenses carry `in_map` (true: one of the mapped papers; false: a cited work outside them, e.g. a
  classic without an English abstract).
- `papers`: every mapped paper's `id`, `group` (0 = in no group), `between`, `x`, `y`.
- `coverage` (`with_references`: how many have references in OpenAlex; `references_thin` when under 65%,
  then the groups lean on wording), `method` (resolution, consensus agreement, ...), `timing`.
`group=N` splits group N of the same map into its own groups. 3–30 s the first time, then cached until the
next data release (`cached: true`). **Counts as 5 requests.** Importance here is local: "core" means cited by
this group's papers, which is the point (what matters to this conversation), not citations overall.

**Reading a group in depth** (counts as 1 request): `read=N` with `part=lists` gives group N's reading lists,
each paper with its abstract; `part=papers&page=1, 2, …` gives *all* of its papers with abstracts, most central
first (most linked to the rest of the group). Add `group=M` to read a group of the split of group M.
As text: `/topics/{question}?read=N&part=lists` (`abstracts=full|short|none`).

**Pages, never cuts.** Text answers are pages of at most ~64k characters (~16-20k tokens: under what AI apps
accept from one call), so nothing is shortened: the map itself (`/topics/{question}?page=2`; page 1 opens with every
group at a glance), a group's lists and a group's papers each come in as many pages as they need. Every answer
says which page it is, how many there are, and what to call next. A busy group of 350 papers is ~13 pages.

**How to use it (agents)**: map first, then read. For a question about a field, call `/topics/{question}`: it
lists every group and every reading list. Then, for every group that bears on the question, read `part=lists`
and every page of `part=papers`: hundreds of abstracts, which a large context holds easily, and which is what
lets you explain the field rather than repeat a ranked list. Split big or mixed groups (`group=N`), search inside
a group with its own phrases, walk citations from its key papers, and answer organised by group.

### GET /map/place?ids=W1,W2&q=...   ·   GET /map/regions   ·   GET /map/counts
Positions on the map of science for up to 200 papers and/or a question; field names, colours and label
positions; exact publication counts per year and subfield. Mostly for drawing maps.

## MCP server

`https://api.sciencemadereadable.com/mcp`: Streamable HTTP, stateless, no authentication; every MCP protocol
revision from 2024-11-05 to 2026-07-28. Answers are Markdown written for a model to read and cite (DOI links,
W-numbers). Tool calls count against the same 30 a minute; over that, the call returns a tool error saying
how long to wait. Opening the address in a browser shows how to add it.

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user science https://api.sciencemadereadable.com/mcp   # Claude Code
codex mcp add science --url https://api.sciencemadereadable.com/mcp                             # Codex
```

Other apps: add a remote MCP server with that address (setup for each: https://sciencemadereadable.com/?api).

| tool | does |
|---|---|
| `search_papers` | /search: `query`, `limit` (1-100), `mode`, `year_from`, `year_to`, `publication_type`, `open_access_only`, `readable_only`, `abstracts` = short (default) / full / none |
| `get_papers` | /works for up to 20 `ids` at once (DOI, W-number, PMCID, URLs): full records |
| `find_similar_papers` | /similar: `paper`, `limit`, the same filters |
| `citation_walk` | /walk: `paper`, `breadth` (neighbours to learn from, default 30), `limit` per section |
| `map_topic` | /topics: `topic`, `papers` (default 1000), `group` (split one group), `year_from`, `year_to`. Every group, every reading list, every expert. Counts as 5 calls |
| `read_topic_group` | /topics with `read`: `topic`, `group`, `part` = lists / papers, `page`, `abstracts` (full by default), `within` (a group of a split). Counts as 1 call |

Also three prompts, `field_overview(topic)`, `literature_review(question)` and `check_claim(claim)`, and this guide
as a resource.

## Result fields

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | OpenAlex W-number, e.g. `W2782456798`; `openalex` is its URL. Use it to cite and to call /works, /similar, /walk |
| `doi`, `pmcid` | identifiers when known (DOI without `https://doi.org/`) |
| `title`, `abstract` | as OpenAlex has them; abstracts can contain HTML/JATS tags |
| `date`, `year` | publication date |
| `type` | article, review, preprint, book-chapter, ... |
| `authors`, `authors_count` | first 12 names joined with `" | "`, and the full count |
| `venue`, `publisher` | journal / repository / book and its publisher |
| `citations` | times cited (OpenAlex, at the snapshot date) |
| `is_oa`, `oa_status`, `license`, `url`, `pdf_url` | open access; links to the landing page and PDF when known |
| `topic`, `field`, `keywords`, `mesh` | OpenAlex's subject labels and MeSH terms (see limits) |
| `pmc_oa`, `pmc_license`, `pmc_type` | PubMed Central open-access copy: present, its licence, article type |
| `smr` | 1 if ScienceMadeReadable can open it: https://sciencemadereadable.com |
| `score` | semantic: cosine similarity (≈0.3–0.7; compare within one search only). keyword: BM25 |
| `junk` | 0–1, how likely the record is spam, an advert or not scholarship (semantic results only) |
| `is_retracted` | always 0 in search results (retracted papers are left out); can be 1 in /works |

## Using it well (for agents)

- **Plain questions go to semantic, precise needs to keyword.** "effects of screen time on toddlers' sleep"
  → semantic. A named gene, drug, acronym, author's exact phrase, or "everything that mentions X" →
  keyword with quotes. For a literature review, run both and merge by `id`.
- **Phrase like a paper, not like a search box.** Semantic search matches writing style too. "how to loose
  weight" pulls in blog-like records; "effectiveness of dietary and exercise interventions for weight loss
  in adults" pulls in trials and reviews. Rewriting a casual question into research language before
  searching is the single biggest quality gain; the junk penalty handles most of the rest.
- **Start from the landscape, not a flat list.** For any question about a field, a topic or "what research
  says": `/topics/{question}` (or `map_topic`) first, then read the groups that bear on it in full
  (`read=N`, `part=lists`, then every page of `part=papers`). Read hundreds of abstracts if needed: that is
  what turns a list of hits into an understanding of the field. Then search inside groups and walk citations.
- **Snowball**: take the best 2–3 results → `/similar/{id}` for more of the same, `/walk?id=` for the
  literature around them. Deduplicate by `id`.
- **Judge papers from the record**: `type` (review vs article), `citations` relative to `year`, `venue`,
  `junk`. Citation counts favour older papers and big fields; do not treat them as quality alone.
- **Save tokens**: `abstracts=false` for screening, then `/works/{id}` only for the papers you keep.
- **Cite** with DOI when present, else the `openalex` URL. Do not invent details the record lacks.
- **Be gentle**: the public door allows 30 requests per minute per address (reading this guide, /docs and
  /openapi.json does not count). Beyond that: HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header (seconds; also
  `retry_after` in the body): wait that long, then retry. A topic map counts as 5. Spend calls well: one search with `k=100` rather
  than several small ones, `abstracts=false` then `/works` only for the papers you keep, never in parallel.

## Limits and honesty

- Search covers English titles + abstracts only (no full texts); papers without an English abstract are
  not in it. Search by meaning reaches back only as far as the coverage above says; exact-word search and
  /works cover the whole corpus.
- Data is an OpenAlex snapshot (see coverage): very recent papers and corrections arrive later.
- `topic` / `field` labels come from that snapshot and are often wrong: OpenAlex has since relabelled more
  than half of a random sample. Don't rely on them for classification; the text is more reliable.
- `junk` is a model (trained on labels from an AI judge, validated on 60 test questions): it pushes
  junk down, but it also pushes down some real papers with thin records (no authors or references listed),
  and it does not judge whether a paper is *right* (crank papers can score clean).
- Errors: 400/422 bad parameters (the body says which), 404 unknown paper or route, 429 too many requests,
  502/503 search briefly unavailable (e.g. during a nightly data update, ~1–3 minutes): retry later.

## Sources

Paper records: OpenAlex (CC0). Full-text flags: PubMed Central (NCBI). Embeddings: DenseOn
(lightonai/DenseOn). Operated for ScienceMadeReadable. Requests (including search words) appear in the
server's request log, which does not record your address.
